results.question: In the cross-sectional pilot study of veterans, what cardiac MRI findings in people living with HIV suggested myocardial fibrosis and subclinical dysfunction?
results.answer: The study reports: "We found higher growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 blood levels, increased extracellular volume, and lower right heart function on MRI among patients with HIV, suggesting the presence of increased myocardial fibrosis and subclinical myocardial dysfunction in this population." [PMID:41791688]. The study reports: "Multivariable linear regressions were used to investigate the associations. 21 veterans with HIV (mean age 54 years; 71% White, 29% Black) and 20 controls (mean age 56 years; 70% White, 30% Black) were included." [PMID:41791688]. Lower right heart function on MRI was found among patients with HIV, suggesting subclinical myocardial dysfunction [PMID:41791688]. The study reports: "We conducted a cross-sectional pilot study of matched veterans with and without HIV receiving care at the Providence VA Medical Center to explore the relationship between systemic inflammation, myocardial fibrosis, and subclinical cardiac disease in HIV." [PMID:41791688]. Limited data from this pilot study suggest that HIV may be associated with increased cardiac fibrosis and decreased right ventricular function [PMID:41791688]. The researchers conducted a cross-sectional pilot study of matched veterans with and without HIV receiving care at the Providence VA Medical Center to explore the relationship between systemic inflammation, myocardial fibrosis, and subclinical cardiac disease in HIV [PMID:41791688].

notes: Contains increased ECV, lower MRI right-heart function, higher GDF-15 and the 21/20 pilot groups; maintains associative scope.

results.resolution: Contains increased ECV, lower MRI right-heart function, higher GDF-15 and the 21/20 pilot groups; maintains associative scope.

results.question: How did the fMRI acceleration method and the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters address different image-reconstruction problems, and what validation result did each report?
results.answer: The study reports: "Our study proposes a novel image reconstruction method to enhance the efficiency of data acquisition while maintaining high accuracy in activation detection." [PMID:41951145]. The study reports: "The through-plane and in-plane acceleration techniques are combined to accelerate image acquisition along two dimensions." [PMID:41951145]. The study reports: "Multiple image-shift strategies and a 2D Hadamard encoding scheme are used to increase encoding diversity and reduce slice leakage." [PMID:41951145]. By applying the approach to both simulated and experimental fMRI data, the method successfully reduced total scan time while achieving a higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in regions of interest (ROI) [PMID:41951145]. The study reports: "Due to the inherent correlation between Rice's noise and the Magnetic Resonance (MR) signal that occurs during the MR images formation, denoising these images is an important but complex process, as it can prove insufficient and even result in the loss of information details." [PMID:41903663]. The study reports: "In fact, in order to denoise MR images with high Rice's noise levels, we propose adapted filtering anisotropic diffusion PDE filter models by using precise local parameters adjustment." [PMID:41903663]. The study reports: "Three unbiased anisotropic diffusion filtering models with optimized parameters for Rician noise removing in MR images.." [PMID:41903663]. The study reports: "These filtering models incorporate a robust Rician noise estimator and an unbiased variant of filters based on anisotropic diffusion, whose parameters are all calculated simultaneously and optimized adaptively through the introduction of the PSO algorithm and the use of reference-based and no-reference quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM and Blind/Referenceless Image Spatial Quality Evaluator (BRISQUE))." [PMID:41903663]. The various tests performed on synthetic and real MR images provided excellent results compared to some other published methods, thus demonstrating the high performance of the proposed filters in terms of noise reduction and preservation of important details [PMID:41903663].

notes: Both actual methods and reported validation findings covered: two-dimensional fMRI acceleration/encoding with simulated and experimental SNR/CNR/time findings; Rician-noise estimation and adaptive PSO diffusion filters with synthetic and real-image noise/detail results. No cross-study superiority.

results.resolution: Both actual methods and reported validation findings covered: two-dimensional fMRI acceleration/encoding with simulated and experimental SNR/CNR/time findings; Rician-noise estimation and adaptive PSO diffusion filters with synthetic and real-image noise/detail results. No cross-study superiority.

results.answer: The study reports: "Higher FV was significantly associated with increased LVMI (mean difference = 22.83; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.37 to 45.29; p = 0.046), whereas dialysis vintage was not (mean difference = 0.51; 95% CI: -0.41 to 1.45; p = 0.27)." [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "A total of 241 patients were included." [PMID:41644509]. The study cannot prove causality or that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes because it was a multicenter cross-sectional study using LVMI as a surrogate marker of cardiovascular morbidity, and multivariate regression models were applied to investigate associations rather than causal effects [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "Left ventricular mass index (LVMI) was used as a surrogate marker of cardiovascular morbidity." [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "Multivariate regression models were applied to investigate the associations of FV and dialysis vintage with LVMI, and to assess potential interactions between these variables." [PMID:41644509].

notes: Complete flow-LVMI contrast including null vintage result, 241 patients and uncertainty; explicitly explains why cross-sectional surrogate associations do not establish benefit from flow reduction.

results.resolution: Complete flow-LVMI contrast including null vintage result, 241 patients and uncertainty; explicitly explains why cross-sectional surrogate associations do not establish benefit from flow reduction.
